headline: 00 scan) -- Explosive-laden drone attacks Iranian Kurdish opposition camp northeast of Erbil, Iraq
dek: An explosive-laden drone attacked an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp northeast of Iraq's Erbil on Saturday, security sources said. No group, casualty figure or damage detail is given in the Reuters item.
sources: Reuters, citing security sources; carried by Arab News and Times of Israel liveblog
fault_line: Is Baghdad able -- or willing -- to stop Iranian Kurdish opposition camps on its soil being struck?

sections.what_happened: An explosive-laden drone attacked an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp northeast of Iraq's Erbil on Saturday, security sources said. No group, casualty figure or damage detail is given in the Reuters item. Context: Rudaw tracking counts 1,000+ drone/missile attacks on the Kurdistan Region by Tehran and Iran-aligned Iraqi groups since Feb 28, with at least 32 killed and 154 wounded as of mid-September; similar camp strikes hit KDPI/Komala/PAK sites on Oct 8, 12, 18 and 21.
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family: Reuters T1 (Arab News and ToI both carry the same Reuters item -- syndication, not independent corroboration).
sections.what_disputed: Attacker is unattributed in the Reuters item -- the pattern points to Iran (per Rudaw tracking and the Oct 21 PAK strike, where Iran's ambassador had just claimed Baghdad agreed to expel the groups, a claim an Iraqi official denied), but attribution for THIS strike is unproven and must not be asserted. No casualty/damage claim is made.
sections.why_matters: Another drone, another Kurdish opposition camp near Erbil -- and once again, no one is named. After 1,000+ such attacks since February, the question is not who fired, but why Baghdad cannot or will not stop it.

totw_analysis: Our read: Another drone, another Kurdish opposition camp near Erbil -- and once again, no one is named. After 1,000+ such attacks since February, the question is not who fired, but why Baghdad cannot or will not stop it. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Baghdad able -- or willing -- to stop Iranian Kurdish opposition camps on its soil being struck?
